@graph.name: Simon Liesinger design system reference
@graph.headline: Simon Liesinger design system | Refero Styles
@graph.description: Explore Simon Liesinger's light Agency design system: Bone #f2f2f2, Graphite #181818 colors, Garamond, Helvetica typography, and DESIGN.md for AI agents.

dos: Use #f2f2f2 for the page canvas and never introduce a different background color within the main content bands
Set all body and headline text in Garamond at weight 400; the serif contrast is the only typographic voice needed
Use #fc523b exclusively for the wireframe illustration and the ↗ arrow glyph — never as a fill on text, buttons, or borders
Separate sections with 1px hairline rules in #181818 or #6e6e6 and 160px of vertical padding rather than cards or backgrounds
Anchor primary navigation to the bottom of the viewport with three text segments divided by vertical rules
Use 0px border-radius on every component — the system is square-cornered throughout
Reserve 12px Helvetica for metadata columns (names, services, contact) and pair it with tabular figures to keep stacked names aligned
donts: Do not add drop shadows, glows, or any form of elevation — the system is flat and reads as printed matter
Do not introduce a second accent color or shift the vermillion to a more saturated or muted red
Do not set body type in Helvetica or display type in Times — the serif/sans division is strictly size-based
Do not use rounded corners on cards, buttons, tags, or images
Do not place navigation at the top of the page or use a hamburger menu
Do not use color blocks, filled buttons, or solid panels as section backgrounds
Do not use font-weight above 400; bold or black weights break the printed-page illusion

colors.name: Bone
colors.role: Page canvas, card surfaces, section backgrounds — the paper of the monograph

colors.name: Graphite
colors.role: Primary text, body copy, hairline rules, column dividers — softer than pure black, reads as printed ink

colors.name: Ink
colors.role: Hardest rule weights, foot dividers, densest border lines — the purest black on the page

colors.name: Ash
colors.role: Muted column rules, secondary divider strokes — the gray that softens the grid

colors.name: Vermillion
colors.role: Link arrows, the wireframe illustration, the only chromatic accent — a printer’s mark red, not an interface brand color

designSystem.layout: Full-bleed page with no max-width container — content stretches to the viewport edges. The page is organized as a vertical stack of horizontal bands, each band subdivided by 1px vertical rules into 3–4 equal columns. The opening statement occupies the top-left in a generous column with the wireframe illustration floating in the center-right space. A four-column metadata band follows (services, services, awards, collaborators), then a two-column prologue block (narrow label column + wide body column), and finally a three-segment bottom navigation. Spacing between bands is ~160px; padding within columns is uniformly 30px. Density is spacious — the grid breathes.
designSystem.imagery: No photography, no raster images. The visual language is almost entirely typographic and structural — the single ornamental element is a wireframe/3D wireframe illustration rendered in thin vermillion (#fc523b) strokes with no fill. Illustrations, when present, are line-based geometric constructions that sit as free-floating objects on the bone canvas. The site’s iconography is limited to the ↗ arrow glyph, which appears exclusively in vermillion.

similar.why: Same monograph-on-the-web treatment: editorial serif body type, generous whitespace, columnar grids, zero ornament beyond typography
Studio portfolio with the same single-accent-color discipline — almost entirely monochrome with one vivid red used sparingly for arrows and small marks
Print-design sensibility applied to web — Garamond-adjacent serif, column rules, flat composition, no shadows or rounded corners
Editorial publishing aesthetic with hairline rules, a single chromatic accent, and typography doing all the structural work

surfaces.name: Bone Canvas
surfaces.purpose: Full-page background, the paper on which everything is printed

surfaces.name: Ink Plate
surfaces.purpose: Dark contrast surface for selected sections or footers

designSystem.northStar: Drafting table on bone paper. A designer’s monograph rendered as a website — serif body type sitting on a vast off-white canvas, punctuated by a single stroke of red.

components.name: Section Column
components.role: Vertical content column within a multi-column grid band
components.description: Full-width band divided by 1px Graphite (#181818) vertical rules into equal columns. 30px horizontal padding per column. No card background — the bone canvas shows through. Headings, lists, and prose stack within the column at 30px top padding.

components.name: Service List
components.role: Left-aligned vertical list of discipline or service labels
components.description: Stacked Garamond 25px or Helvetica 12px items separated by 12–14px of vertical space. No bullets, no dividers between items — whitespace carries the rhythm. Left-aligned to the column edge.

components.name: Collaborator Roster
components.role: Right-side column listing names and disciplines
components.description: Two-line pair: name in Helvetica 12px weight 400, discipline label in the same size immediately below, separated by tight line-height. Names carry an asterisk marker (★ or *) to flag them. Tabular figures keep the names optically aligned in a column.

components.name: Bottom Navigation
components.role: Primary site navigation anchored to page foot
components.description: Three segments — about ↗, work ↗, lab ↗ — set in Garamond, separated by 1px Graphite (#181818) vertical rules. Arrow glyph rendered in Vermillion (#fc523b). 30px horizontal padding, ~79px bottom padding from viewport edge.

components.name: Link Arrow
components.description: Vermillion (#fc523b) diagonal arrow (↗) trailing a text label. The only place the accent color touches text. Functions as a signifier of navigation away from the current context.

components.name: Wireframe Illustration
components.role: Decorative centerpiece in the hero region
components.description: Geometric line drawing in Vermillion (#fc523b) — thin 1px strokes, no fills, transparent. Sits as a free-floating ornament on the bone canvas. The only non-textual, non-structural element on the page.

components.name: Prologue Block
components.description: Indented label 'prologue' in 12px Helvetica sits in a narrow left column; the body text occupies a wider right column at Garamond 25px with 40px bottom margin before the next band. Generous left margin (119px) creates the indentation.

components.name: Contact Strip
components.role: Email and phone metadata at page foot
components.description: Two-line stack: 'hello@liesingers.com*' and '+43 (0)650 68 98 665*' in Helvetica 12px, Graphite (#181818). Tightly packed against the bottom-left of the viewport.

components.name: Section Divider
components.description: 1px Ash (#6e6e6e) or Graphite (#181818) hairline spanning the full viewport width. 160px of vertical padding above and below creates the breathing room between sections.

components.name: Heading Statement
components.description: Garamond 36px weight 400, line-height 0.86 (tight), set left-aligned. The tight leading is a deliberate editorial choice — lines almost touch, creating a compact monogram-like block.

typography.role: Editorial serif used for headlines, body copy, and the introductory address. Set exclusively at weight 400 — the typeface’s contrast and oldstyle proportions do the visual lifting. The 36px tier is the opening statement, 29px is section copy, 25px is dense paragraphs.

Small UI metadata — navigation labels, contact lines, service labels, collaborator names. Renders with tabular figures and stylistic alternates (ss04, ss07, zero) so columns of names align like a typeset index.
typography.substitute: Inter, Neue Haas Grotesk, Helvetica Neue

typography.role: Micro-copy at 10px — copyright, fine print, the smallest annotations. System serif fallback for the tiniest type tier.

designSystem.description: Liesingers is a gallery-wrapped-in-a-browser: a near-monochromatic editorial portfolio where a warm vermillion red is the only chromatic interruption in an otherwise graphite-and-bone-white composition. The system behaves like a printed monograph — Garamond sets the voice for headlines and body copy, while Helvetica with tabular figures handles the metadata column at the foot of the page. The grid is unapologetically wide and columnar, sections stack as full-bleed bands separated by hairline rules, and the navigation lives at the bottom rather than the top. Components are flat, borderless in the traditional sense, and rely on line weight and whitespace for structure rather than fill, shadow, or color blocks. The wireframe illustration in vermillion is the only piece of ornament — everything else earns its place as structure or text.
designSystem.elevationPhilosophy: No shadows. No elevation. Structure is communicated exclusively through line weight, column rules, and whitespace. The system trusts the grid.
